title: Raspberry Shake Event Detection vs Local Noise
app: Raspberry Shake, Safecast, Blitzortung-compatible lightning sensors, AirGradient CO2 sensors, radon monitors, allsky cameras, and magnetometers streamed to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=seismo:reading
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(noise_floor) as noise_floor, count(eval(event_detected=1)) as detected_events by station _time
| where detected_events>0
| sort - detected_events
description: Uses Raspberry Shake telemetry telemetry to monitor detected events alongside the local seismic noise floor in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for whether the sensor is seeing interesting events or just living in a loud spot, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Raspberry Shake telemetry data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a hourly cadence.
visualization: Daily station table of noise floor and detected events.
grandmaExplanation: It lists detected events alongside the local seismic noise floor so you can spot whether the sensor is seeing interesting events or just living in a loud spot before it becomes annoying.
